newsitem.title: USA: U.S. House tax conferees give on smaller items. [CORRECTED 01:15 GMT]
newsitem.headline: U.S. House tax conferees give on smaller items. [CORRECTED 01:15 GMT]

text.p: House tax negotiators in a first offer Tuesday proposed accepting Senate provisions in the more minor areas of tax legislation such as reducing taxes on cider.

In the major areas House conferees did not make a move away from their tax bill including on the $500 per child tax credit, education tax incentives, estate tax relief, expanded Individual Retirement Accounts and a capital gains tax cut, according to a copy of the offer.
House and Senate lawmakers are trying to work out differences in their legislation to form one final tax bill.
(Corrects to remove a paragraph incorrectly referring to alternative minimum tax provision).

On the cider tax, House conferees proposed going along with the Senate proposal to reduce the tax rate on apple cider having an alcohol content of no more than seven percent to 22.6 cents per gallon, the same as for beer. Currently cider is taxed at the same rate as wine of $1.07 per gallon.
The House offer also went along with a Senate provision directing the Treasury Department to conduct a study related to collection of the distilled spirits excise tax.

House conferees offered to accept the Senate's date to delay imposition of penalties on small businesses for failing to make payments of certain taxes to Treasury electronically to after June 30, 1998, rather than after Dec. 31, 1998.

House tax negotiators also offered to defer to the Senate on the effective date for allowing computer software licensed for reproduction abroad to receive an export benefit that would allow a portion of the foreign trade income to be exempt from federal income tax. The House had originally phased in the exemption, but offered to go with the Senate effective date of after December 31, 1997.
